Title: Python Library Bug Triage — numfmt 2.4.1
Time: Friday 22 March, 15:00–16:00 (UTC), Room 4B + Zoom

Hey team,

We've had four separate reports this week that numfmt 2.4.1 raises a KeyError when formatting negative decimals with a thousands separator, e.g. numfmt.fmt(-1234.5, sep=",") blows up instead of returning "-1,234.5". I've reproduced it on Python 3.11 and 3.12, so it's not an environment quirk. The upstream maintainer has acknowledged it but hasn't given a timeline.

This hour is for triage: decide whether we pin to 2.4.0, patch a local fork, or work around it in our exporters, and who owns each of those. I'll walk through the minimal repro and the two candidate patches I sketched. If you already have a workaround in your service, bring the code snippet.

We'll also do a five-minute look at whether the docs assistant's suggested fix (strip the sign, format, then re-add) is actually correct — I'm not convinced it handles the percent path. Notes will go into the engineering wiki afterwards.

Cheers,
Dana

Title: Bug Bash — Negative Number Formatting
Time: Thursday 4 April, 10:00–12:00, Room 4B

We're spending the morning hammering on the number-formatting edge cases before the 2.4.2 release: negatives, percent, thousands separators, and locale variants across de-DE and fr-FR. Title: API Deprecation Town Hall
Time: Tuesday 16 April, 15:00–16:00 (UTC), Auditorium + livestream

All hands for the platform group. As announced, the v3 Feeds API retires on 30 June and we've now published the v4 migration guide. This town hall walks through what changes, what we've made easier, and the support channels available if you get stuck.

Agenda:

1. Why we're deprecating v3 and what the timeline looks like (15 min, Marcus)
2. Live walkthrough of the v4 migration path, including auth token changes (20 min, Priya)
3. Q&A — submit questions in the form beforehand or ask in the room (15 min)
4. Office hours schedule and how to book a 1:1 (5 min)

The recording and slides will be posted in the platform channel within 24 hours. If you own any service still calling v3, this is the one session I'd ask you to prioritise; the migration guide, the endpoint mapping table, and the sandbox credentials are all linked from the invite description. Note that the sandbox has a monthly quota and we've had a couple of teams burn through it early, so request a key rather than sharing one. Questions to the platform-announce mailbox please, not the general one.

intent.requested_action: attend a town hall about an API deprecation
